No service layer or external data loading path is present in the included source. The supplied smoke tests cover fixture presence and currency formatting, not route interactions. Inferences: The fixed, small local fixture and lack of asynchronous loading provide no source evidence of a performance bottleneck, so no performance defect is asserted. Several narrow-screen overflow findings below are inferred from CSS minimum widths and overflow rules and were not rendered. Hypotheses: Actual viewport behavior and dynamic interaction outcomes remain unverified.

Notifications and the supported Overview and Analytics exports call a status toast that hides after a timeout. Orders search and status filters update the result count and render an empty row when nothing matches; the View action reveals order details. specialist_assessments.assessment: The overview has a clear, consistent operations-dashboard identity across all three viewports. The desktop layout presents the greeting and actions first, then four KPIs and two side-by-side information panels. Tablet and mobile retain the same palette and typography while progressively stacking content. No visible rendering failure is apparent in the supplied screenshots. The main subjective refinement is that the mobile first viewport is dominated by the KPI stack, leaving the revenue trend and recent activity below the fold.

evidence.description: Desktop view: dark sidebar and white top bar frame a spacious canvas. The greeting and actions lead into four KPI cards, then the revenue chart and recent activity panels.
Tablet view: the top bar uses a menu icon, the KPI cards form a two-column grid, and the chart takes the full content width before the next panel begins.
Mobile view: the greeting and two actions fit above a single-column stack of KPI cards; the fourth card continues past the bottom of the captured viewport.

limitations: The assessment uses only the three supplied screenshots. It does not assess content below the captured viewports or interaction states.
The mobile screenshot shows only the initial viewport, so the report describes the visible KPI emphasis without judging the full-page mobile experience.

specialist_assessments.assessment: The supplied screenshots support a consistent, restrained dashboard design: pale cool-gray workspace, white bordered cards, dark blue-gray text, and teal accents. The desktop uses a full-height dark sidebar; tablet and mobile show a compact top bar with a menu icon. At mobile width, the KPI stack dominates the captured content, with only three cards fully visible and part of the fourth; the trend and activity panels are below the captured viewport. The implementation supports the observed reflow: the KPI grid changes from four columns to two below 1180px, the content panels stack at that breakpoint, the sidebar moves off-canvas below 800px, and the KPI grid becomes one column below 520px (assets/styles.css:2, assets/styles.css:7-9; index.html:3, index.html:6-7).
